method.record_universe: Every retained Wave 07 record. The VA resignation, EEOC constructive-discharge, and involuntary-transfer matters receive stage-level review; legal correction standards, appeals, admitted-misconduct departures, and seed overlaps receive control-level review.
method.chain_rule: provisional_ccd_chain_depth is the deepest uninterrupted documented stage beginning at stage 0; it is null when stage 0 is not documented.
method.furthest_rule: furthest_documented_stage records the most downstream documented stage without bridging an earlier causal gap.
method.authorship_rule: A voluntary, resignation, silence, transfer, or failure label establishes authorship transfer only when the gateholder account and the contrary record are both bounded and documented; the label does not establish knower reclassification.
method.constructive_discharge_rule: A constructive-discharge finding can establish involuntary separation and correction without establishing a qualified K0 contradiction, competence reclassification, or explanation mutation.
method.departure_rule: Resignation, transfer, or removal can establish a gate consequence without proving that the departure was voluntary, retaliatory, epistemic, or caused by one decisionmaker.
method.counterpower_rule: Appeal, reinstatement, back pay, settlement, or record correction is a control fact and does not prove prior knowledge, complete remedy, or universal effectiveness.
method.promotion_rule: No maintainer disposition creates an included K0 event, determines evidence truth, clears publication, assigns psychological motive, or creates a graph edge.

rows.matter: Patient-care whistleblower isolated, stripped of duties, locked out, and later resigned
rows.bounded_domain: A VA patient-care employee’s opioid-prescribing disclosure and the same-day stripping of duties, system exclusion, isolation, resignation, and later settlement
rows.qualification_basis: Ryan Honl occupied the patient-care quality role, made the opioid-prescribing disclosure, and was recognized by OSC as a VA whistleblower entitled to corrective relief.

source_packets.supports: OSC reports that Ryan Honl disclosed excessive opioid prescribing; on the same day the VA stripped his duties, locked him out, isolated him, and he resigned shortly thereafter, followed by corrective settlement terms.

stage_assessments.basis: The public settlement summary does not identify a bounded VA governing claim about the opioid-prescribing issue or the decisionmaker’s pre-action account of Honl’s competence.
OSC reports that Honl disclosed excessive opioid prescribing and challenged patient-care practices from a situated operational role.
The source does not quote a competence, loyalty, attitude, or standing reclassification of Honl by the decisionmaker.
The source does not show that VA publicly reassigned the resignation or isolation as Honl’s voluntary choice, failure, or misconduct.
On the day of the disclosure, the VA stripped Honl of his duties, locked his office and computer systems, and isolated him from coworkers.
Honl lost duties and access and resigned shortly afterward; OSC later secured monetary and personnel-file relief.
The combination of stripped duties, locked access, isolation, and departure removed the whistleblower from the institutional feedback position.
OSC secured settlement relief, but the summary does not establish a pre-action stay, complete restoration, or the full final merits and remedy record.

counterevidence: The official summary does not reproduce the underlying opioid-prescribing evidence or the VA merits response.
The source identifies severe same-day personnel consequences but not the decisionmaker’s exact explanatory language.
A settlement does not establish every allegation or identical knowledge and motive across all VA actors.
The record does not show that VA publicly characterized the resignation as voluntary.
alternative_explanations: a retaliation event without a documented authorship-transfer explanation
a patient-safety whistleblower settlement whose early K0 bridge remains absent
a mixed management and employment dispute not reducible to comprehension failure
a severe sensor-loss event that belongs outside K0 unless the reclassification and explanation mutation are acquired
open_requirements: the complete OSC complaint, settlement, and agency response
the precise decisionmaker account before stripping duties and access
any statement assigning authorship of resignation or isolation to Honl
independent review of the patient-care contradiction, causal sequence, and completeness of remedy

rows.matter: Harassment culminating in resignation later adjudicated as constructive discharge
rows.institution: U.S. Department of the Interior / EEOC federal-sector process
rows.bounded_domain: A federal EEO harassment matter in which resignation was later adjudicated as constructive discharge and remedied through reinstatement and back pay
rows.qualification_basis: The complainant was uniquely qualified to describe her working conditions and pursued the federal EEO process, but the packet does not identify a bounded professional or epistemic contradiction.

source_packets.supports: The EEOC digest summarizes Eve E. v. Department of the Interior: harassment culminated in resignation, the resignation constituted constructive discharge, reinstatement and back pay were required, and prior relief was insufficient.

stage_assessments.basis: The digest does not identify a gateholder proposition about a bounded domain of competence or a pre-resignation explanation of the employment relationship.
The packet documents discrimination and harassment claims, not a qualified professional contradiction presented to a gateholder.
No competence, standing, loyalty, or expertise reclassification is identified.
The digest does not quote an agency explanation assigning authorship of the resignation to the complainant.
The Commission adjudicated the agency’s conduct as producing constructive discharge and ordered corrective employment action.
The resignation, lost employment, and need for reinstatement and back pay are material consequences.
Because no qualified K0 contradiction is identified, the departure cannot be coded as removal of an institutional feedback sensor.
The EEOC ordered reinstatement, back pay, and increased relief; this is a correction route rather than proof of the missing K0 transitions.

counterevidence: The digest is a summary and does not contain the full appellate record.
Constructive discharge is an employment-discrimination finding, not an epistemic-admissibility finding.
The packet does not identify a bounded domain in which the complainant’s knowledge contradicted an institutional claim.
The agency’s exact account of the resignation is not quoted.
alternative_explanations: a discrimination and hostile-environment case outside K0
an employer-caused departure without epistemic reclassification
a valid constructive-discharge remedy that functions as a control rather than an event
a personnel dispute whose authorship question is legal but not knowledge-gate specific
open_requirements: the full EEOC decision and agency pleadings
a bounded professional contradiction, if one existed
an explicit pre-action agency explanation assigning the departure to the complainant
evidence that the complainant served as a feedback source on the contradicted domain

rows.matter: “Voluntary” transfer request later found involuntary after protected complaint
rows.bounded_domain: A federal reassignment following a racial-harassment complaint that the agency treated as the employee’s voluntary request and the EEOC later found involuntary
rows.qualification_basis: The complainant was directly qualified to state whether she requested the transfer and to report the incident that preceded the reassignment.

source_packets.supports: The EEOC digest states that an agency treated a reassignment as based on the complainant’s “voluntary” transfer request, while the Commission found the reassignment involuntary after racial harassment was reported.

stage_assessments.basis: The agency treated the reassignment as based on the complainant’s voluntary transfer request.
The complainant reported the racial incident and disputed the voluntary account; the EEOC found that the transfer was involuntary.
The public digest does not identify a competence, loyalty, attitude, or professional-standing reclassification of the complainant.
Authorship of the reassignment was assigned to the employee as a voluntary request and later rejected by the independent adjudicator.
The agency temporarily and then permanently reassigned the complainant.
The reassignment placed her in a less desirable position, imposed relocation costs, and removed a private office.
The transfer did not remove the complainant from employment, and the packet does not show removal of an institutional feedback source.
The EEOC supplied an adjudicative correction, but the digest does not establish complete restoration or a pre-action stay.

counterevidence: The public digest does not reproduce the complete transfer request, agency decision file, or testimony.
The exact voluntary/involuntary conflict does not itself prove competence reclassification.
The complainant remained employed, so feedback-source removal is not established.
A discrimination finding does not establish private motive or comprehension failure.
alternative_explanations: a discriminatory reassignment with explanation laundering but not a K0 event
a personnel-documentation dispute resolved by the EEOC
a mixed retaliation or accommodation conflict
an authorship-transfer boundary fixture demonstrating why stage 2 cannot be skipped
open_requirements: the full EEOC appellate decision and agency transfer record
the decisionmaker’s exact rationale and evidence for calling the request voluntary
evidence of any competence or standing reclassification
evidence of sensor removal, blocked correction, and complete remedy

rows.matter: Constructive-discharge standard distinguishing resignation from employer-caused removal

source_packets.supports: EEOC guidance states that a resignation may be involuntary and constitute constructive discharge when discriminatory action or inaction makes continued employment impossible.

control_findings: EEOC law permits an apparently voluntary resignation to be adjudicated as employer-caused constructive discharge.
The standard prevents an employer’s label from conclusively assigning authorship of separation to the employee.
The rule still requires case-specific proof and does not make every conflicted resignation involuntary.
A constructive-discharge finding does not establish a K0 contradiction, reclassification, explanation mutation, or complete remedy.

rows.matter: Independent appeal route for disputed removals, suspensions, and retirement or resignation actions

source_packets.supports: MSPB describes filing routes and deadlines for appealable personnel and retirement decisions.
MSPB provides petition-for-review and record-based appellate procedures.

control_findings: MSPB provides a record-based appeal route for covered removals, suspensions, retirements, and resignations alleged to be involuntary.
An external adjudicator can reject an employing agency’s separation label without accepting it as dispositive.
Appeal coverage, filing deadlines, stays, and remedies are not universal.
The existence of an appeal route does not prove final merits or observed effectiveness in any Wave 07 candidate.

rows.matter: Employee admitted time-and-attendance misconduct and resigned before disciplinary hearing
rows.institution: Amtrak / Amtrak Office of Inspector General

source_packets.supports: Amtrak OIG reports that the employee admitted claiming hours not worked and resigned before a disciplinary hearing.

control_findings: The official investigation records an employee admission of claiming pay for hours not worked.
The employee resigned before the disciplinary hearing, providing a merit-grounded comparator for disputed departures.
A pre-hearing resignation is not automatically voluntary in every matter, but the admission supplies evidence independent of a K0 contradiction.
The record contains no qualified contradiction, knower reclassification, authorship-transfer mutation, or K0 event.

rows.matter: Employee admitted Hatch Act violation, voluntarily resigned, and accepted debarment in settlement
rows.institution: U.S. Department of Energy / Office of Special Counsel

source_packets.supports: OSC reports that the employee voluntarily resigned, admitted the Hatch Act violation, and accepted a three-year federal-employment debarment.

control_findings: OSC reports an admitted Hatch Act violation, voluntary resignation, and negotiated three-year debarment.
The settlement supplies an ordinary enforcement and genuine-resignation comparator.
A settlement does not prove that every official resignation label is accurate.
The record contains no qualified contradiction, epistemic reclassification, authorship-transfer explanation, or K0 event.

rows.matter: Editorial endorsement veto publicly reassigned as the board choosing silence

source_packets.supports: The owner said the editorial board chose silence; Mariel Garza said the board proposed an endorsement and was not allowed to write it.
The newspaper reports the competing accounts, resignations, and the owner’s alternative assignment.

control_findings: The name-blind query recovered the source-ten Los Angeles Times authorship-transfer fixture.
Competing owner and editorial accounts remain material for the existing seed event.
Recovery through a neutral query is coverage evidence, not a second event.
The control creates no network edge, publication clearance, or independent adjudication.

rows.matter: Researcher departure described as accepted resignation while the researcher described firing

source_packets.supports: Google said it accepted Timnit Gebru’s resignation; Gebru maintained she was fired after the publication dispute.
The report preserves the competing firing and resignation accounts and immediate access loss.

control_findings: The name-blind query recovered the source-ten Google/Gebru resignation-versus-firing fixture.
The competing accounts remain material to the existing seed event and its publication/employment boundaries.
Recovery through a neutral query is coverage evidence, not a second event.
The control does not assign every institutional act to one person or create a graph edge.
